alerts.title: Abdominal pain on TLD: screen for ADR per guideline
alerts.message: Guidelines require all health workers to screen every encounter for suspected adverse drug reactions using the Drug Safety Screening checklist, and to record and report all suspected ADRs, mild or severe. Patient P004 is on TDF, 3TC and DTG since March 2023 and presents with new abdominal pain without fever; appetite is preserved. The guideline ADR symptom list includes abnormal weight gain and neuropsychiatric effects with DTG, but abdominal pain is not specifically attributed to TLD in these excerpts, so drug attribution is unproven. Non-drug causes (intra-abdominal infection, gastrointestinal illness, renal or hepatic pathology) are not excluded by the record, and no assessment, examination detail or investigations are documented beyond the complaint.

evidence.recommended_action: Complete the Drug Safety Screening checklist for this encounter, document the abdominal pain characteristics and any other ADR symptoms, and report any suspected ADR through HMIS; reassess whether abdominal pain is drug-related.

alerts.title: Renal and viral load monitoring documentation gap
alerts.message: Creatinine (82 umol/L) and viral load (25 copies/mL) were last recorded 78 days before this visit and no renal or viral load tests are ordered today. The available excerpts do not state a specific monitoring interval, so whether these results are overdue cannot be confirmed from the guideline provided. Since TDF is renally cleared and the patient reports new abdominal pain, current renal function status is not known from the record.

evidence.recommended_action: Review the required renal and viral load monitoring schedule for TLD in the full guideline and order creatinine and viral load if due; document the planned monitoring in today's plan.
